title: Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions, Part II: nonordinary CM special values
summary: This roadmap supplies the nonordinary complex special values and normalized elliptic-unit reciprocity needed at an inert prime of an imaginary quadratic field. It proves the auxiliary-character, root-number, conductor, period and coefficient comparisons behind the local optimal-unit argument. Its main unit theorem specializes Finis at an inert valuation prime without assuming ordinary CM reduction. General elliptic units, Hecke characters and Lubin–Tate theory retain their existing owners.
readme: The definitive reader is research/blueprint/readmes/NonordinaryCMSpecialValues.md. The six layers form the early special-value branch. AnticyclotomicLocalUnits consumes it; Rubin interpolation and the primitive Iwasawa coordinate belong to InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture. The complete planning pass records explicit supplier and source obligations; no implementation or dependency closure is asserted.

stages.title: CM periods and auxiliary characters
stages.description: Fix the actual CM Gross Q-curve, its good differential and a principal complex period lattice; compare the dual/Tate conventions with Kato. Compute the positive canonical root number when 2 splits. Choose a split auxiliary l with p∤(l−1), and define the finite anticyclotomic characters with separate order, layer and conductor indices.

stages.title: Normalized elliptic-unit reciprocity
stages.description: Specialize the single shared elliptic-unit foundation to BKO’s chosen integral rank-one lattice and Betti vector. Prove the direct-character semilocal dual-exponential formula, its period-change law and the norm-compatible inverse-limit twist comparison. The unsmoothed fraction-module class is not silently treated as integral.

stages.title: Torsion towers and the CM Lubin–Tate comparison
stages.description: Form the actual torsion/ring-class composita. Prove disjointness by ramification and l∤h_K, complete splitting of p in prime-to-p ring-class fields, and the semilocal factorization used for character evaluation. Apply the existing Honda/Lubin–Tate theorem to the CM curve after calculating Frobenius as [−p].

stages.title: Root numbers and forced central zeros
stages.description: Prove that auxiliary l-power twists preserve the root number. For nontrivial p-anticyclotomic characters of conductor p^c, prove W(φνχ)=(−1)^c W(φ), using the local Fröhlich–Queyrut root number of the anticyclotomic character at p. Deduce opposite-parity zero values through the actual Hecke functional equation, with the trivial character separate and without any signed local-unit freeness theorem.

stages.title: Finis’s inert-prime unit specialization
stages.description: Construct the Finis family λ=barφν/N and verify its self-duality, infinity type, central point and conductor. Switch Finis’s tower prime to l and his valuation prime to p; calculate all inert μ terms and b_p to be zero. Compare the same good period, including the p-unit discriminant factor, remove the ramified l factors, and obtain almost-all p-unit normalized values and a nontrivial witness.

stages.title: General nonvanishing and coefficient descent
stages.description: Prove the arbitrary-class-number central nonvanishing input through Jia’s Galois-average argument: the fixed-support average with main term 2L(1,κ_R), invariance of the root number under Aut(C/K), Rohrlich’s lattice-point bound derived from the p-adic subspace theorem, and Galois stability of vanishing through the weight-two CM newform and the coefficient-embedding comparison of modular critical values. For canonical data prove that the coefficient field is unramified at p and that the normalized values lie in unramified fields, by Kato’s reciprocity at prime-to-p level; then compare scalar and tensor character kernels using total ramification of the Lubin–Tate levels. Export this restricted repair to the local-unit consumer while retaining the ramified-coefficient limitation.
